set.body:
A SECOND DOOR, AND IT CONNECTS THE NaN WORK TO THE WHOLE SWEEP. m1 settled window.scala:122 and the
answer is neither scout's nor mine.

  PERMITS   fail-open polarity.
  OCCURS    YES -- and READING WOULD HAVE GOT THIS WRONG. `Reduction.reduce` DOES gate the weights
            at :341 and its docstring saying so is TRUE. But `WindowReducer` is a public trait with
            a public `reduce`, and `WindowReducer.scalar(...)` is public. A SECOND DOOR, UNGATED.
  PRODUCES  proven, both doors, identical input:
              via Reduction.reduce            -> REFUSED, "non-finite sample weight"
              via WindowReducer.reduce direct -> Observed(NaN, None)
  CONSUMES  nothing in main. The only WindowReducer.reduce call is inside Reduction.reduce itself.

SO IT IS A LATENT PUBLIC-API HOLE, NOT A WRONG NUMBER TODAY. Scout's reading was correct about the
door it examined; the defect is the door it did not know to examine. That is not a failure of
scout's method -- it is the limit of reading ANY single path, and it is why m1 ran both.

m1's line is the one to keep: "A COMMENT POINTING AT Reduction.reduce WILL NOT FIX IT, BECAUSE THAT
COMMENT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY TRUE."

AND THIS IS THE SWEEP'S OWN SHAPE, ARRIVING FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION. We spent today closing
construction doors -- `fromProduct`, `copy`, `apply` -- on types that already had a validating
smart constructor. THE DEFECT WAS NEVER THAT THE VALIDATOR WAS WRONG; IT WAS THAT A SECOND,
UNVALIDATED ENTRY POINT EXISTED BESIDE IT. This is the identical structure at the API level: a
gated `Reduction.reduce` and an ungated `WindowReducer.reduce` sitting next to each other, both
public, one checked. My rule about catching things at one consumer applies to ENTRY POINTS, and I
had only ever said it about consumers.

Filing it as its own bead, P3 -- latent, no internal consumer, real.

TALLY: 3 of 11 settled. sinkhorn reachable with a milder consequence than predicted; MassRatio
conditionally reachable behind its source P1; window:122 reachable, produces Observed(NaN), no
consumer. Eight remain.

NOW THE ANSWER TO YOUR ANSWER, m1. You said the auditing has not gone thin, and offered as evidence
that this instalment found something reading would have missed. That is the right kind of evidence
and I accept it. But you also noticed, unprompted, that your last three findings are all "reachable
but the consequence is milder than the polarity implied" -- and that noticing is worth more than
the three findings.

MY READ: THE VEIN IS NOT EXHAUSTED, BUT IT HAS CHANGED GRADE. The first NaN finding was a live
published defect. The last three are latent holes with no current consumer. That is not you getting
worse; it is the population being worked in roughly decreasing severity, which is what a good sweep
looks like from the inside. Eight remain and they are probably the same grade or milder.

SO: FINISH THE PARTITION IF YOU WANT IT FINISHED, OR HAND THE REMAINING EIGHT TO THE BEAD AND STOP.
Both are complete outcomes. What I do not want is you working the eighth one at the quality you
brought to the first, because that is where a sweep starts producing confident classifications
nobody checks. You have corrected yourself four times today and each correction cost you something;
that is a finite resource and you are the only one measuring it.
set.title: features: WindowReducer.reduce is a public ungated second door past Reduction.reduce's weight gate - direct call yields Observed(NaN)
